gloss: holing up; besieging oneself in a castle; staying indoors

definitions.gloss: besieging oneself in a castle; holding out in a fortification
definitions.explanation: The historical military strategy of shutting oneself inside a castle or fortress to defend against attackers. A key concept in Japanese feudal warfare.

definitions.gloss: holing up; shutting oneself in; staying indoors for an extended period
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, staying inside a building or room for a long time without going out. Used for studying intensively, working on a project, or refusing to leave.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}に{籠城|ろうじょう}する。
examples.english: To hole up in the castle.

examples.japanese: {兵糧|ひょうろう}{攻|ぜ}めで{籠城|ろうじょう}は{長|なが}く{続|つづ}かなかった。
examples.english: The siege did not last long due to a food blockade.

examples.japanese: {籠城戦|ろうじょうせん}で{半年間|はんとしかん}{持|も}ちこたえた。
examples.english: They held out for half a year in a siege.

examples.japanese: {試験前|しけんまえ}は{家|いえ}に{籠城|ろうじょう}する。
examples.english: Before exams, I hole up at home.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}りが{近|ちか}いので{週末|しゅうまつ}は{籠城|ろうじょう}だ。
examples.english: The deadline is approaching, so I'm holing up this weekend.

examples.japanese: {図書館|としょかん}に{籠城|ろうじょう}して{論文|ろんぶん}を{書|か}き{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: I holed up in the library and finished writing my paper.

notes: Composed of {籠|ろう} (to be confined, basket) + {城|じょう} (castle). Takes する: {籠城|ろうじょう}する. Historical compounds: {籠城戦|ろうじょうせん} (siege warfare), {籠城|ろうじょう}{作戦|さくせん} (siege strategy). The figurative use (sense 2) is very common in modern Japanese, often humorous or self-deprecating. Also written as {篭城|ろうじょう} with the simplified kanji.
